text:
maya: quick report — trying to wire OTEL into our async sample app and hit two things: (1) background tasks launched with `asyncio.create_task` end up with new trace ids, (2) the AsyncClient stubs are typed as returning `str` which is misleading.
sam: thanks for filing. which python + sdk version?
maya: python 3.10, redwood-py 0.9.2 from pip. repro sketch below. parent span exists, then i kick off a background job that calls `client.generate` and that call appears as a separate root span (new trace id).
lee: this smells like contextvar propagation. when you call `asyncio.create_task` the current Context is not copied into the new task on 3.10, so the OTEL current span isn't available there.
dena: fwiw our SDK currently injects trace headers on outbound HTTP calls if one is present in the request context, but if the SDK starts a new root span because no context was found you'll get a different trace id.
maya: minimal repro: ```python
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient
from opentelemetry import trace

client = AsyncClient(api_key="x")
tracer = trace.get_tracer("demo")

async def handler():
    with tracer.start_as_current_span("parent"):
        # background work - create_task loses context on 3.10
        asyncio.create_task(client.generate(prompt="hello"))

asyncio.run(handler())
```
sam: two immediate asks: (A) small doc note + sample explaining `create_task` caveat, and (B) a helper in the SDK to preserve context when scheduling background coroutines.
lee: design for the helper could be `client.create_task_preserve_context(coro)` which under the hood uses `ctx = contextvars.copy_context(); ctx.run(lambda: asyncio.create_task(coro))` or when available uses `asyncio.create_task` variants on 3.11+.
dena: +1. also request: add a config toggle on AsyncClient like `propagate_traceparent_header: bool` so infra teams can opt into propagating the raw `traceparent` header downstream for cross-service correlation.
maya: typing problem: stub files show `async def generate(...) -> str` but it returns a coroutine that resolves to a `GenerateResponse` dataclass. mypy and IDEs get confused. can we fix stubs to `-> Awaitable[GenerateResponse]` or annotate with `async def generate(...) -> GenerateResponse` (since async def implies coroutine)? either way current mismatch causes dev friction in examples.
sam: agreed. i'll open a typing PR. goal: make async methods have precise runtime return types and ship type stubs that match. also add small typed models for responses in `redwood.types`.
lee: another instrumentation request: expose an `OTelInstrumentation` helper that registers attributes on spans like `redwood.model.id`, `redwood.request.tokens_in`, `redwood.request.tokens_out`. should be pluggable with OTEL auto-instrumentation.
dena: sample app would be great — minimally: (1) quick example showing `create_task_preserve_context`, (2) OTEL setup + example exporter (console), (3) sampling toggles and explanation, (4) tiny test that asserts trace ids propagate across tasks.
ci-bot: created issue devex/py-sdk#4234: "async context propagation helper + typing + otel attrs" assigned to @sam.
sam: timeline: i'll push a draft PR tonight with docs + helper + example under `examples/telemetry/async_context.py`. follow-up for types + instrumentation next sprint.
infra: ping from infra — if you add `propagate_traceparent_header` please default to false and ensure we don't leak internal trace ids for hosted customers without consent. also include a strongly-worded doc snippet for security teams.
maya: perfect. thanks all. will validate the sample app once PR lands and paste feedback here. :rocket:
